decisions.statement: Every calculation is answered in this one answer.
The pages acted on are every page property a function works out.
A page whose type is written by nothing is passed over.
A calculation already naming that type is passed over.
The type named is the one written beside the property.
The page the calculation takes is left as the calculation names it.
The type is named beside whatever else the calculation takes that shape from.
A code file exporting no such calculation is refused rather than passed over.
A slug making no type name refuses the change before any code is composed.
The path the type is imported from is written as the source spells a string.
A run every calculation of which names that type already is refused as no edit.
One page's code is changed by two edits over the one body.
One page refused refuses the whole change, and the refusal names that page.
A folder named holds the change to the pages sitting under that folder.
Nothing here reads what kind a property states.

definition: every calculation naming its own property's type rather than restating that kind
